title: J. C. Heard, his protege
summary: He met young drummer J. C. Heard at the Rhythm Club, mentored him, and later brought him to Cannes; he also recalls 1975 records.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: But did you know that one night I needed a drummer--I was working in a place called the Checker Barbecue and I needed a drummer and I was in the Rhythm Club. And this kid was there, little straw hat and had his drums in a paper bag. His snare drum. And I asked him his name and he said, 'J. C. Heard.'

And J. C. Heard from that moment on became one of my protégés. And he used to have a problem of raising his tempos ... you know, he used to rush his tempos. But he went on to become one of the all-time greats as a percussionist, to be rated along with Jo Jones and those guys ; and played with all kinds of bands...Cab Calloway, Café Society, Jazz at the Philharmonic and I was so proud that one year I took him to Europe for a festival in Cannes and he...I took him to this festival in Cannes and we had Sidney Bechet and Coleman Hawkins, Roy Eldridge, and he was the only one that received an award at this festival. And it was because they only had one drummer and he had to do all of the playing. So I said to the impresario, "you got to do something special for him," so they gave him an award. But I'd rate J. C. as one of the all time greats. I'd rate him as one of the all-time greats. He was a nice guy.

And to hear him play with Dorothy Donegan was...she was fantastic and so was he, so...I think that you'd consider that... I'd consider it and classify it as a game of skill, have the two of them playing together, you know, as they did. As recently as 1975 I made some records with J. C. and Doc Cheatham, with Ted Buckner before he died--Milt Buckner's brother. And, who else did we have. We had...who did we have on bass?... DM: George Duvivier?
No, we didn't have George Duvivier, we had a guy they called "The Bruiser." I can't remember his name but I can
give it to you later. But he was a...
Speaking of bass players from Detroit, was Major Holley around?
No, Major Holley wasn't...he was around, perhaps, but he wasn't out there. You know, he wasn't that well known. He wasn't well known.
